newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: STRONG MINE UNION VITAL TO S.AFRICA'S FUTURE - NUM.
newsitem.headline: STRONG MINE UNION VITAL TO S.AFRICA'S FUTURE - NUM.

text.p: South Africa's economic future and a better life for miners hinged on a strong National Union of Mineworkers, NUM president James Motlatsi said on Wednesday.

"I believe that a strong and militant NUM is vital for the political future of our society, the transformation of the mining industry in the interest of our members and for the economic future of the country as a whole," Motlatsi told the union's congress.
Black miners in South Africa should be employed on terms comparable with advanced Western mining nations, he said.

Motlatsi said that while South African wages for black miners compared favourably with wages received by miners in third world countries, South African companies should be offering wages similar to those in advanced mining nations, with which South Africa shared technology and development.
"I want the same standards to be applied to our members. I want black mineworkers here to have the pay, conditions and status equivalent to the best in the world," Motlatsi said.
He urged members to continue waging a class struggle through political and industrial action.
Striking should only be used as "a weapon of last resort" after negotiation to resolve differences with employers and government has failed, he added.
"But we should always keep it (striking) bright, shiny and sharpened, ready to use at any minute," he said.
Motlatsi also said that the NUM needed to become more efficient and serve its members more effectively.
"I am aware that our organisation could be much more efficient than it is and that we do not, in consequence, serve our members effectively," he said.
